newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Du Plessis eyes Australian back row.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Du Plessis eyes Australian back row.

text.p: South Africa's rugby union coach Carel du Plessis on Wednesday identified Australia's revamped back row as a potential weak spot in this weekend's meeting between the two Tri-Nations rivals.
"They will certainly be under pressure in that department of their game," du Plessis told reporters during a break from training for Saturday's test in Brisbane.

Wallaby coach Greg Smith, reacting to his side's 33-18 defeat against Tri-Nations leaders New Zealand on Saturday, recalled flankers David Wilson and Matt Cockbain and switched Daniel Manu from breakaway to number eight.
ACT Brumbies captain and flanker Brett Robinson and number eight Michael Brial lost their places in the latest back row reshuffle, the fifth in six internationals so far this season.
"I believe Australia will try to secure priority first phase (possession) and set it up from there. Only if they can create that will they be able to bring their backs into play," du Plessis said.
"They've got a lot of attacking ability out wide but the question will be if they can set the platform from the forwards," Du Plessis said.
The changes mark yet another round of tinkering by Australia selectors in their search for an effective and settled scrum.
Of the forwards, only lock and captain John Eales has been picked for all six home tests. Fourteen other players have been used to fill the other seven positions.
"Now it's outright desperation," screamed a headline in Wednesday's The Australian newspaper, commenting on Cockbain's switch from his normal lock position in only his second test.

The Springboks, in contrast, have opted for consistency by making only one change to the side that lost 35-32 to the All Blacks in the series opener on July 19, naming prop Dawie Theron to replace Marius Hurter.

Wallaby fly-half David Knox, recalled as a replacement for injured Tim Horan, said he did not welcome past comments by Smith, who cited a lack of defensive ability for previously overlooking the stylish ACT Brumbies playmaker.
"It's not nice to hear those sort of things," Knox said.
"But I hate it (my tackling) being overstated all the time. I know it's not my strong point but I don't think they are bringing me back for my defence.
"Hopefully I'll get the chance to maybe get the backline going and throw a few balls around," he said. REUTER
